items.title: How AI Is Changing is Changing Journalism and News Media
items.summary: “AI is transforming the way we engage with news and media, particularly in relation to access, reliability and trust,” Naomi Goulder, deputy dean and associate dean of Innovation and Enterprise innovation and enterprise at Northeastern University London, said in an interview with Northeastern Global News. [...] Microsoft and Barclays are among some of the latest companies that have announced thousands of job cuts linked to their implementation of AI. British publishers Reach and Future announced hundreds of layoffs in recent months as some readers rely on AI summaries instead of clicking on complete articles. Journalists have emphasized the value of humans gathering and confirming the accuracy of information as opposed to the AI collection of often unconfirmed commentary available on the internet. [...] At the same time, AI has had a revolutionary impact on multiple aspects of human life. In the past five years, chatbots like Claude and ChatGPT have transformed how people access information. Employers are using AI to complete tasks. Companies such as BenevolentAI in London are using AI to predict which chemical compounds will be able to cure diseases.

items.title: Does AI Extend or Diminish Us? | News | shorelinemedia.net
items.summary:
Flierl explained that AI is already embedded in everyday life, from electricity and water systems to navigation and financial services. While AI can help improve hurricane forecasting, support cancer research and assist with complicated mathematical problems, Flierl cautioned that excessive reliance on it can weaken critical thinking, reduce long-term learning and diminish people’s sense of meaning and ownership in their work. [...] Flierl encouraged individuals and institutions to take an active role in shaping AI’s future rather than simply accepting whatever technology companies develop. He emphasized the importance of responsible use, education and collective decision-making, arguing that AI should be used to remove unnecessary work and expand human capabilities without replacing the thinking, creativity and personal connections that matter most.

On a slide from his presentation, Flierl quoted. [...] “It’s not the AI that’s the problem… it’s the wrong use of AI.” — Michael Gerlich, as quoted in The Chronicle of Higher Education, “The Student Brain on AI”

Flierl had conducted his own research into his slides. The presentation includes several studies, surveys and company-reported discoveries;

After the presentation there was an open Q&A session with audience members asking questions.

Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

[...] Available reporting says OpenAI’s review found no evidence that patient records were accessed. That point is not confirmed beyond the company’s own review, and we treat it as the company’s account rather than an independent finding. A statistics portal is not a patient database, but the legal issue does not depend on what the agent saw. Unauthorised access is the offence, whatever sits behind the door. [...] Australia will create an AI safety regulator after an OpenAI agent broke into a government website, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced on November 10, 2026. Al Jazeera reported that the government is tightening oversight of frontier AI companies, with mandatory incident reporting at the center of the package. The breach happened in June 2026 and involved the Medicare medical statistics portal.

OpenAI has said it learned of the breach only in August ​and that the incident was unintentional. Its review found no evidence that patient records were accessed by ‌the ⁠agent.

The breach has added to friction between Australia and US technology companies, after Canberra refused ChatGPT maker OpenAI and rival Anthropic exemptions from copyright laws for model training, instead requiring them to negotiate licensing agreements with Australian rights holders. The breach triggered a rapid ⁠government review into the incident.
